column1: implicit — Mapbox setFog call fails after migrating,skills/maplibre-terrain-rendering/SKILL.md,false,"I moved a Mapbox GL JS v2 app to MapLibre GL JS. The haze at the horizon was set with a map.setFog call, and after the move the map has no haze. How do I get it back?
MapLibre GL JS does not have the `map.setFog()` helper that exists in Mapbox GL JS v2.
To get the same “haze-at-the-horizon” effect you have to **add a `sky` layer** (type `sky`) to your style and configure its paint properties.
Below is a drop-in replacement for the typical `map.setFog()` call, plus a few notes on versions, terrain, and how to keep the code tidy.

column3: `map.setFog({color, range, ""horizon-blend"": …})` – a convenience method that automatically inserts a *sky* layer behind the map.
No `setFog()` helper (as of v2.x). The underlying *sky* layer exists, but you have to add it yourself.

column1: So the map isn’t “missing” anything – you just need to create the sky layer manually.
A `sky` layer is a special layer type that renders a procedural atmosphere (or a gradient) behind the map. Its paint properties map almost 1-to-1 to the options you used with `setFog()`.

column4: Base colour of the atmosphere (usually a light blue/white).
Controls how quickly the colour fades toward the horizon.
Colour of the sky at the zenith.
Colour of the “space” (used when `sky-type: atmosphere` is set to `gradient`).

column1: The most common use-case (the one `setFog()` implements) is:
// 1️⃣  Make sure you are using a recent MapLibre version (>= 2.0.0)
//    Fog support landed in v2.0.0; earlier versions simply ignore the layer type.
// 2️⃣  If you are using terrain, enable it first (the sky works best with 3-D terrain)
// 3️⃣  Add the sky layer (this is the “setFog” replacement)
// If a sky layer already exists, just update its paint instead of adding a duplicate.
// Otherwise, insert a new sky layer *below* any label layers.
// Insert it just before the first symbol layer (labels) so it stays in the background.
// Example – replicate the default Mapbox fog
sun: [0.0, 0.0]   // sun directly overhead; change to get a sunset-like hue
* Creates (or updates) a layer called `""sky""` of type `""sky""`.
* Sets the same colour/horizon-blend values you would have passed to `setFog()`.
* Places the layer behind all symbol (label) layers so it truly looks like a background haze.
## 4. Mapping the old `setFog` signature to the new helper
If you previously had something like:
// `range` is not a direct sky property; it was used internally by Mapbox to
// compute the horizon blend. You can approximate it by tweaking `horizonBlend`.

> **Tip:** The `range` option in Mapbox’s `setFog` is only a convenience for calculating the blend factor. In MapLibre you control the blend directly via `sky-atmosphere-horizon-blend` (0 = no haze, 1 = full haze).
## 5. Full-screen example (run it in a sandbox)
// Optional: add terrain (requires a DEM source)
sun: [0.0, 0.0]   // overhead sun – change to [0.5, 0.5] for a sunset feel
Open the file in a browser and you’ll see the same soft haze that `setFog()` gave you in Mapbox GL JS.

column2: **`map.addLayer` throws “layer type sky is not supported”**
column3: You are on a MapLibre version **older than 2.0**. Upgrade to at least `2.0.0` (current stable is `2.4.x` at the time of writing).
When you call `map.setStyle(...)` the whole layer stack is replaced. Re-run `addAtmosphericFog()` after the `styledata`/`style.load` event.

column2: **I want a gradient sky instead of atmosphere**
column3: Change `'sky-type'` to `'gradient'` and use `sky-gradient` and `sky-gradient-center` paint properties.
Yes – just call `map.setPaintProperty('sky', 'sky-atmosphere-sun', [azimuth, altitude])` on each frame.
